rejected.title: Chronic respiratory adaptations
card: Chronic adaptations are lasting changes from weeks to months of regular aerobic training. The breathing muscles, such as the diaphragm, get stronger and tire less easily.
At maximal exercise, tidal volume (air moved in one breath) and ventilation (air moved per minute) rise. More air reaches the alveoli each minute.

At rest and at submaximal intensities, respiratory frequency (breaths per minute) falls and ventilation can fall. Each breath is deeper and more oxygen is taken from it, so breathing costs less energy.

More capillaries form around the alveoli, so pulmonary diffusion (gas exchange) improves. With heart and muscle changes, this helps raise VO2 max, the most oxygen the body can use per minute. A higher VO2 max raises the ceiling, not the oxygen a set pace needs.
rejected.remember: Trained breathing is slower and deeper at rest, bigger at maximum, and better at moving oxygen into the blood.

a.q: Compared with before months of aerobic training, which pattern would you expect in a trained athlete?
opts: Lower breathing rate at rest, more ventilation at maximum
Higher breathing rate at rest, more ventilation at maximum
Lower breathing rate at rest, less ventilation at maximum
Same breathing rate at rest, lower tidal volume at maximum
a.why: At rest, deeper breaths and better oxygen extraction mean fewer breaths are needed. At maximal effort, tidal volume and ventilation rise so more air reaches the alveoli. Expecting less ventilation at maximum is tempting, but that only applies at rest and submaximal levels.
a.clue: The change at rest and the change at maximum go in different directions.

b.q: After six months of aerobic training, Tariq rows at the same submaximal pace as before but takes fewer breaths per minute. What best explains this?
opts: Each breath is deeper and more oxygen is taken from it
His VO2 max rose, so he needs less oxygen at that pace
His tidal volume fell, so each breath takes less effort
His diffusion fell, so less air is needed per minute
b.why: Training makes each breath deeper and improves how much oxygen is taken from it, so fewer breaths meet the same need. The VO2 max option is tempting, but VO2 max is the ceiling at maximal effort and does not lower the oxygen a set pace needs.
b.clue: Look at what changes within each breath, not the maximum.

draft.title: Chronic respiratory adaptations
card: Chronic adaptations are lasting changes that build up over weeks and months of regular training. Aerobic training changes how the lungs and breathing muscles work.
The breathing muscles, such as the diaphragm, get stronger. Tidal volume (the air moved in one breath) and minute ventilation (the air moved in one minute) rise during maximal exercise.
Gas exchange gets better. More oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood, so the body can take in and use more oxygen.
VO2 max is the highest rate at which the body can use oxygen. It rises with aerobic training. At submaximal intensities, breathing becomes more efficient and needs less effort.
draft.remember: Aerobic training makes breathing stronger and more efficient, which helps lift VO2 max.

a.q: After months of aerobic training, which change would be expected in the respiratory system?
opts: Stronger breathing muscles and better gas exchange
Fewer alveoli so less air is lost
A permanently lower VO2 max
Weaker diaphragm because it works less
a.why: Aerobic training strengthens breathing muscles and improves gas exchange, so more oxygen reaches the blood. The idea that muscles weaken from work is the reverse of what happens, as regular use makes them stronger.
a.clue: Think about what regular use does to a muscle.

b.q: Tariq, a Melbourne rower, trains aerobically for six months and retests his VO2 max. What is the most likely result?
opts: VO2 max rises as oxygen use improves
VO2 max stays the same as lungs cannot adapt
VO2 max falls as breathing gets easier
VO2 max rises only if he stops training
b.why: Aerobic training improves breathing and gas exchange, so the body can use more oxygen and VO2 max rises. Saying the lungs cannot adapt is tempting, but the card shows that breathing muscles and gas exchange both change.
b.clue: Consider what better oxygen intake does to the highest rate of oxygen use.

a.best: Stronger breathing muscles and better gas exchange

b.best: VO2 max rises as oxygen use improves
